title: E2 — calls issued by code in bursts: how closely agents start (W-code, H6)
description: W-code (ADR-037): sweep of the window in which the agents start (startSpreadMs; 0 = an orchestrator spawning every sub-agent at the same instant), with every agent issuing its 16 calls in steps of 4 calls sent at once, waiting for all of them, then thinking for one model turn before the next step. The burst size 4 is an assumption between the sizes of e2-code-burst. Assumptions, none measured and none tuned on results: 8 agents; 16 calls per agent; the shared catalog, Zipf exponent and overlap of the W-syn base (50 documents, 0.8, 0.5); a model turn between steps with an exponential think time of mean 2 s; surface variation 0, because arguments written by code are built mechanically (loop variables, ids copied from an earlier result) and vary less in spelling than model-written ones; links, service time, result sizes, TTL and Content Store as the W-syn base. The shape (calls issued from code, several per model turn, in parallel) is documented for programmatic tool calling and Code Mode; how often such calls repeat across agents has not been measured by anyone, so this sweep shows the mechanism, not a measured workload. Same seeds at every point; reductions are paired by seed against B0, B1 and B5 (ADR-036).

source.statistic: median over runs of the per-run median (p50_us), microseconds
